articles.title: France needs 'more public services', 'salaries are too low', 'schools are in very, very bad shape'
articles.feed_excerpt: As France confronts another wave of strikes and protests, Gaëlle Martinez, National Secretary of the trade union Solidaires, presents the general strike as more than a confrontation over wages, public spending or the cost of living. Her account reveals a deeper struggle over economic dignity, the future of public services and the democratic right to collective protest. “People just want to live, not survive.” For Martinez, deteriorating schools, insufficient salaries and the dismantling of public services are not isolated policy failures. They are interconnected symptoms of political and economic priorities that, in her assessment, place fiscal restraint above social welfare. Her demand for “a new budget” that is “not based on cuts” is accompanied by a call to “tax the biggest companies, the richest companies where the profits are made.”

articles.feed_excerpt: The BLVD is home to 250 enterprises, from banks, tattoo shops and restaurants to museums and a performing arts centre Passing through the Mojave desert on State Route 14, going by landscapes Hollywood uses to represent alien planets, a driver might not expect to find a walkable, tree-lined boulevard. But there are nine beautiful, leafy blocks on West Lancaster Boulevard, a piece of what used to be Highway 14. They were redeveloped as part of a mixed-use urban streetscape in the city of Lancaster, California in 2010. The BLVD, as it’s been rebranded, is home to 250 public and private enterprises, from banks, tattoo shops and restaurants to museums, a performing arts centre and a public library. City Hall is just a block south. The city invested $11.5m (£8.5m) to transform a busy thoroughfare into an inviting public space. The three lanes in the centre of the former five-lane road were replaced by a series of tree-lined ramblas – Spanish for “avenue” and “watercourse,” because dry stream beds served as streets in early cities. The redesign was planned and funded by the city of redevelopment agency. Within four years of completion, it had generated more than $270m in economic output, attracted $130m in investment, created hundreds of jobs and prompted the building or renovation of hundreds of housing units, according to the city. The revitalisation has also created more intangible benefits, residents say. The city centre the feels like a gathering space, they said — somewhere where they can feel like part of a community. articles.title: 運輸及物流局舉行解讀「十五五」規劃與香港五年規劃航空業研討會
articles.feed_excerpt: 運輸及物流局舉行「解讀《民用航空發展十五五規劃》與《香港五年規劃》航空業研討會」。國家民用航空局副局長韓鈞率團到港，和本地約100個航空業界機構代表交流。中聯辦經濟部部長徐衛剛亦有出席。 運輸及物流局局長陳美寶在研討會致歡迎辭，感謝國家民航局代表團遠道而來，以及中聯辦的大力支持，讓香港的航空業界以第一身角度了解國家發展策略。她又提出支持國家「暢通國際運輸通道」、深化大灣區多式聯運，提升樞紐高質量發展，及深耕專業與高端航空服務，為國家民航引進全球創新要素三個工作重點，呼籲業界全力規劃服務國家宏大布局的戰略支點。 韓鈞致辭時，闡述國家民航局「十五五規劃」對深化民航高質量發展的戰略意義，並對香港航空業界的熱烈參與表示謝意。 多名航空業界機構代表亦在會上分享各自對貫徹落實「十五五規劃」和「五年規劃」的相應部署。機構代表和國家民航局代表團與特區政府團隊，在會場內外都作出深入交流。 編輯：陳樂謙

articles.title: ‘Children were wearing fake life jackets’: one Syrian family’s terrifying, 10-year journey
articles.feed_excerpt: In 2015, two film-makers first met 11-year-old refugee Israa, forced to abandon Aleppo for a new life in Europe, along with her parents and siblings. None of them imagined what would come next In 2015, an 11-year-old Syrian girl called Israa matter-of-factly explained how her family would survive if their dinghy sank crossing the sea from Turkey to Greece. Her father would grab her disabled sister; her mother would look after the baby. “And I,” said Israa, a huge smile lighting her face, “I know how to rescue myself.” Wife-and-husband documentary-makers Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes met Israa while filming a BBC series, Exodus , about refugees trying to reach Europe. Their plan was to follow Israa and her family on their hazardous journey to Germany. But after Israa reached safety, the pair kept filming. Ten years in the making, their documentary, One in a Million, is extraordinary - with echoes of Richard Linklater’s Boyhood and the Up! series . We watch Israa grow up in front of our eyes, from a sunny-natured 11-year-old to a woman, married with a baby of her own. Continue reading...

articles.title: I Play Rocky review – Anthony Ippolito adds knockout sweetness to the story of Stallone’s Hollywood triumph
articles.feed_excerpt: Portraying the humour, passion and grit that took the actor from bit parts to Oscar glory, this making-of tale is even more mythic than the original movie For fun, excitement and the transcendental thrill of success, there’s nothing to touch this very enjoyable drama about the making of Sylvester Stallone’s Oscar-winning 1976 boxing movie, Rocky. It’s a movie of duplicates and surfaces and heartfelt imitations. Perhaps not very profound but, as Oscar Wilde’s Lord Henry Wotton says, it is only shallow people who do not judge by appearances. It is the story of the struggling young Italian-American unknown who’d had some minor acting jobs – including softcore pornography – but wrote a thumpingly good screenplay inspired by the underdog white boxer Chuck Wepner , who briefly knocked Ali down in 1975. With tremendous self-belief, Stallone insisted he play the lead role himself, holding out against vast cash offers to just take the writing credit and let an established star into the ring. articles.title: 謝振中：香港媒體可為內地企業出海提供品牌策劃及市場推廣等服務
articles.feed_excerpt: 政府新聞處處長謝振中表示，《香港第一個五年規劃》提到，要增加主流媒體國際傳播能力，而連續兩年的《施政報告》都提及特區政府會協助本地傳媒發展香港以外的網絡，說好香港故事。 謝振中在社交媒體表示，在上海舉行的第九屆進博會，貿發局向全球商家展示「出海專班跨界別專業服務平台」，羅列八大領域的出海服務供應商，可滿足內地企業出海的各方面需要。他表示，內地企業要出海，需要做品牌推廣工作，香港本地媒體擁有兩文三語能力和國際視野，極具創意和市場觸覺，正好可為內地企業提供品牌策劃、市場推廣、國際形象管理等服務。 他表示，貿發局的平台已納入4間本地傳媒機構，清晰展示服務範圍、受眾版圖、海外服務經驗等，相信既能協助內地企業精準匹配資源，亦可讓本地媒體一展所長，發揮專業優勢拓展出海業務，是雙贏的合作模式，有助加強國際傳播軟實力。 編輯：陳樂謙

articles.title: Jimmy review – simple-minded James Stewart biopic is too straightforward
articles.feed_excerpt: Riverdale’s KJ Apa gives surprisingly solid performance but this corny look at actor’s life is missed opportunity The last time the New Zealand actor KJ Apa took on a midcentury American pop-cultural icon, he was playing a nominally sexy yet often weirdly bloodless version of Archie Andrews, the feckless teen nextdoor on the comic-book riff Riverdale. He also frequently ceded scenes to his scene partners, whether former teen idols like Luke Perry or newer, more dynamic personalities like Camila Mendes or Madelaine Petsch. Now he’s taking on an even more beloved and therefore trickier part: James Stewart, the Pennsylvania-accented avatar of decency who starred in dozens of classic films and spent decades as a box office mainstay. Yes, Archie has been promoted to a Jimmy Stewart biopic. The movie, called just plain Jimmy, focuses on Stewart’s willing military service during the second world war and its immediate aftermath. Here, Apa is in far less danger of being outshone by his co-stars; it’s competing memories of the real Stewart, available through so many great, good and watchable-because-of-him movies, that he has to worry about. The substantial and perhaps only surprise that Jimmy has up its sleeve is that Apa does a reasonable imitation of one of the most immediately distinctive movie stars of all time. Plenty of people can approximate that famous voice, less clipped and urbane than so many of his co-stars, but Apa gets some of his gangly physicality, too. articles.title: 李家超陪同丁薛祥巡視進博會香港展區 介紹香港最新發展
articles.feed_excerpt: 行政長官李家超表示，很高興出席第九屆中國國際進口博覽會開幕式，感謝國家對香港的大力支持，並在進博會中國館設置香港展區。 李家超表示，陪同國務院副總理丁薛祥巡視香港展區時，介紹展區特色及香港最新發展。他表示，在國家大力支持下，香港經濟發展態勢良好，在各領域重要國際排名均取得佳績，充分顯示國際社會對香港充滿信心，亦介紹在9月公布的《香港第一個五年規劃》，推動香港主動對接國家「十五五」規劃，更好融入和服務國家發展大局。李家超表示，香港將把握好優勢，鞏固提升國際金融、航運、貿易中心及國際航空樞紐地位，加快建設國際創新科技中心，打造國際高端人才集聚高地，實現經濟社會高質量發展。 李家超表示，下午出席虹橋國際經濟論壇香港分論壇，並參觀進博會企業商業展，為參展的香港企業打氣。展館提供多元化推廣配套，包括「直播間」、內地主播探店帶貨、廚藝示範和試食、參展商分享會及商貿配對等，讓香港企業直接與潛在內地客戶交流，提升內地知名度並帶來實質商機。他鼓勵香港企業留意今年《施政報告》協助企業拓展內地市場和提升香港出海平台功能的政策措施，把握國家發展帶來的龐大機遇，憑藉「香港製造」和「香港高增值專業企業服務」的金漆招牌，開拓更廣闊市場。 編輯：陳樂謙

articles.feed_excerpt: Surreal, mysterious and with an outlandish origin story, Jan Potocki’s The Manuscript Found in Saragossa has amassed a cult following that includes Salman Rushdie and Jerry Garcia. But it’s the book’s global humanism makes it relevant now, say the curators of a new exhibition A young Walloon officer called Alphonse van Worden travels through the Sierra Morena on his way to Madrid to join the Spanish army. Along the way he has an erotic encounter with two demonic Moorish sisters, falls foul of shape-shifting apparitions and is tested by a Jewish Kabbalist attempting to use mystical formulas to control spirits and decipher the universe. All these things happen in what might be one of the least-known great novels of the European canon, an encyclopedic roman-monde written more than 200 years ago called The Manuscript Found in Saragossa. articles.title: 澳門首宗國安案將於明早宣判
articles.feed_excerpt: 澳門首宗國安案在明早10時宣判。公眾可以在今日下午4時後到初級法院，憑澳門居民身份證，以一人一籌，先到先得，記名領取旁聽證。 根據初級法院安排，傳媒在4時前的一小時內，要辦理旁聽採訪證，因法庭的傳媒旁聽席數量有限，會以澳門記者優先和採取先報先得方式。 澳門首宗涉嫌違返《維護國家安全法》的案件，在9月以閉門方式開審，並已完成案中被告區錦新涉危害國家安全案件的庭審程序，擇日宣判。 區錦新是澳門前立法會直選議員，去年9月因涉嫌觸犯國家安全法被捕，今年7月初完成初審，9月16日以閉門方式開庭審訊，以３日審結。 編輯：譚佩貞

articles.title: Black Doves review – Ben Whishaw, Keira Knightley and Sarah Lancashire are spine-tinglingly good
articles.feed_excerpt: Series two of this rambunctiously entertaining espionage drama might be implausible. But it’s a magnetically acted tale of friendship, with moments of genuine poignance Is Helen Webb Britain’s busiest mum? Or Britain’s least busy mum? On the one hand, she’s got two kids, is the wife of the recently promoted prime minister and also a deep cover spy, who spends her days passing information about her husband’s work to a shady intelligence organisation and her nights on covert missions which often involve acts of bloody slaughter. Yet the reason she can do all this is that nobody expects her to do anything at all: she doesn’t have to look after her children (she has an ever-present nanny – who, unbeknown to Helen, is in fact another spy), manage the household, hold down a job or even sleep in her own bed at night. Forget getting away with murder – how does she get away with not doing the school run?! I don’t think you’re meant to spend Black Doves obsessing over Helen’s domestic arrangements, but if you like cataloguing the ways spy dramas stretch credulity to its absolute limits, Joe Barton’s thriller will certainly scratch that itch. This is a show so relentlessly preposterous it’s practically nihilistic: not just because Black Doves’ excessive body count makes life itself look cheap and worthless, but because searching for coherence in its bewildering storylines quickly starts feeling like a waste of time too. articles.title: 外交部重申堅定支持香港特區依法維護國家安全
articles.feed_excerpt: 前香港眾志秘書長黃之鋒承認一項串謀勾結外國或者境外勢力危害國家安全罪，被判囚10年。 在北京，外交部發言人郭嘉昆表示，香港是法治社會，有法必依，違法必究是基本原則，黃之鋒犯有串謀勾結外國或境外勢力危害國家安全罪，罪行嚴重，在大量事實和證據面前無從狡辯，選擇認罪。 郭嘉昆重申，中國中央政府堅定支持香港特區依法維護國家安全，打擊危害國家安全的行為，呼籲有關方面切實尊重中國主權、尊重香港法治，停止就特區司法案件審理發表不負責任的言論，停止以任何形式干預香港司法、干涉中國內政。 編輯：盧曉珊

articles.title: 外交部：中期選舉是美國內政 願繼續與美方維護落實元首共識
articles.feed_excerpt: 在北京，外交部發言人郭嘉昆在例行記者會被問到，中美兩國在美國中期選舉後的關係。郭嘉昆重申，中期選舉是美國的內政，中方願意繼續與美方維護好、落實好兩國元首重要共識，加強溝通，妥處分歧，拓展合作，構建基於尊重、公平、對等的中美建設性戰略穩定關係。 另外，商務部發言人黃玲回應有關進口美國農產品的問題時表示，中美農產品貿易是雙邊經貿合作的重要組成部分，中方一直對擴大從美國採購農產品，持開放態度，但前提是雙方達成的「300億對300億」對等降稅安排落地。希望美方與中方共同努力，透過降低關稅、減少非關稅壁壘、擴大市場准入等方式，為兩國農產品貿易創造更多有利條件。 編輯：盧曉珊

articles.title: 王文濤：支持香港在國際經貿合作發揮更大作用 盡早加入RCEP
articles.feed_excerpt: 第九屆虹橋國際經濟論壇香港分論壇下午舉行。商務部部長王文濤在視像致辭表示，商務部將積極支持香港發揮背靠祖國、聯通世界的獨特地位和重要作用，鞏固提升競爭優勢，更好融入和服務國家發展大局，助力香港將首個五年規劃願景圖轉化為發展實景圖。 王文濤表示，將支持香港進一步發揮高度自由開放、國際聯繫廣泛、專業服務發達等優勢，加快構建高增值供應鏈服務中心，深化國際法律及解決爭議服務中心、區域知識產權貿易中心等建設，打造數字貿易、綠色貿易、離岸貿易等新業態的示範通道。 他表示，正與特區政府一道共同推動CEPA新一輪升級。一是以服務業為重點，聚焦金融、航運、科技創新等領域，進一步擴大對香港開放，探索更多邊境後開放舉措；二是促進互聯互通，支持大灣區發揮先行先試作用，促進要素高效便捷流動，推動內地與香港規則規制、管理標準相通相融。 王文濤又說，將支持香港在國際經貿合作發揮更大作用，對外商簽經貿協定，盡早加入RCEP，豐富區域合作的制度性安排。另外，將支持香港發揮超級聯繫人、超級增值人作用，深入參與高質量共建一帶一路，為國家對接全球市場、擴大開放合作、參與全球治理搭建重要橋梁。 編輯：譚佩貞

articles.title: American Hagwon by Min Jin Lee review – a gloriously immersive follow-up to Pachinko
articles.feed_excerpt: A Korean family is willing to sacrifice everything for their children’s education, in the third book in Lee’s Diaspora Quartet “An excellent hagwon,” according to one of the characters in Min Jin Lee’s new novel, “is everything.” Every year, Korean parents pay hefty sums to send their children to these private after-school academies designed to turbocharge academic performance, where they spend evenings and weekends being drilled in mathematics, reasoning and essay technique. In the third book in what she has called her Diaspora Quartet – a follow-up to 2017’s Pachinko , recently named one of the New York Times’s top 100 books of the 21st century – she presents the fierce competition to snag a spot at those hagwons deemed the best as symptomatic of Korea’s scarcity mindset: in a country where university places and white-collar jobs are hard to come by, everyone’s looking for an edge. But over the course of the novel’s 650 pages, they also come to stand as symbols of pretty much everything you can think of: of country and culture; of failure and success; of responsibility, or the lack of it; of what it means to achieve, and of what, in the final analysis, the purpose of our achievements might be. The action in American Hagwon unspools over nearly three decades, and crisscrosses from Seoul to Sydney to California and back to Seoul again. At its centre is the Koh family: John, Helen and their three children, Bo, DH and Mido. When the novel opens in 1992, their life in Korea appears comfortably middle-class – John is a senior manager at a multinational corporation; Helen is an upmarket saleswoman, her commissions covering the children’s hagwon fees. But they are dramatically capsized: first by a personal betrayal and then again, in a brutal one-two, by the financial crisis

articles.title: Being Heumann review – stirring biopic of a pioneering disability rights campaigner
articles.feed_excerpt: Heartfelt real-life drama follows the late activist whose groundbreaking struggle helped build a rainbow alliance with gay action groups and the Black Panthers The remarkable story of the late US disability rights campaigner and wheelchair user Judy Heumann – pronounced “human” – is the subject of this heartfelt if Hollywoodised story from director and co-writer Sian Heder, based on Heumann’s own 2020 memoir of the same title. In the lead is British actor Ruth Madeley , who has spina bifida and is herself a disability rights activist; she gives a forthright, smart, sympathetic performance. Heumann’s finest hour was to get the federal government to sign into law Section 504 of the 1973 Rehabilitation Act , whose accessibility provisions had been resisted by Nixon, Ford and then Carter. In 1977, Heumann led a guerrilla sit-in occupation of the San Francisco Health, Education and Welfare offices, her group being a rainbow alliance including gay action groups and the Black Panthers. Secretary of State for Health Joseph Califano sensationally conceded and signed the bill that he and the political establishment had obstructed for years. He is played by Mark Ruffalo, whose nice-guy persona and one-note performance of exasperated detachment does however rather obscure the fact that in real life, Califano at first personally authorised moves to starve the protesters out. In the movie, this grim political decision is not explicitly dramatised. Continue reading...

articles.title: What Do Verifiable Rewards Teach Video-Language Models About Time? A Controlled Multi-Model Study
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2610.03792v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) has produced large reasoning gains in language models, and verifiable video benchmarks make the recipe directly applicable to causal-temporal video question answering. We present a controlled study of what RLVR actually teaches video-language models about temporal structure. We fine-tune four open models with group relative policy optimization (GRPO) under three data recipes using annotated synthetic questions, self-supervised real-video pretext tasks, and a one-to-one mixture, plus a targeted real-video augmentation arm. We evaluate the model-recipe grid on 105 CLEVRER questions with one correct option and on two real-video transfer sets. The 8B ordered gain is 4.8 points (95% video-bootstrap CI [-5.6, 15.1]), while blind accuracy increases 10.5 points ([0.9, 20.6]). The 4B model gains an accuracy advantage for ordered over shuffled frames. On the real-video sets, the 8B synthetic-only checkpoint loses 26.7 and 25.2 points, with smaller regressions under mixed and augmented recipes. In a separate scene-disjoint, single-gold Qwen3-VL-8B experiment, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and GRPO each complete 1,200 updates at three fixed seeds. GRPO minus SFT is -3.89 points in ordered accuracy (nominal 97.5% video-bootstrap CI [-7.36, -0.45]) and -2.78 points in ordered-minus-shuffled accuracy ([-6.60, 0.87]). Transfer differences are sensitive to parseability. Intervals quantify test-video uncertainty conditional on the fitted runs. The results show why benchmark accuracy, transfer, and presented-order sensitivity need to be evaluated separately.

articles.title: Driving Video Retrieval for Complex Queries with Structured Grounding
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2606.09109v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Video retrieval at scale is central to data curation and safety validation in autonomous driving, where users want to find not only scenes but also dynamic events such as cut-ins and hard braking. Existing vision-language and keyword-based retrieval methods often miss these events because the relevant motion may not be explicitly described in text or captured by lexical overlap. Rule-based retrieval can encode such events more directly, but it is brittle: generated or hand-written rules often fail when their assumptions do not match real driving data. We propose STRIVE-D, a data-calibrated retrieval framework for driving videos. It uses weakly labeled in-domain videos to estimate when a query rule is reliable, adapt rules that mismatch observed data, and fuse calibrated rule scores with vision-language and keyword-based retrieval signals. Across three driving benchmarks, including newly released human-annotated event data on DrivingDojo, STRIVE-D delivers up to 84% relative improvement in top-1 accuracy over state-of-the-art methods.

articles.title: NodeSyn: Socially Aligned Synthetic Data for AI Evaluation
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2605.14381v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent advancements in generative AI facilitate large-scale synthetic data genera- tion for model evaluation. However, without targeted approaches, these datasets often lack the sociotechnical nuance required for sensitive domains. We introduce NodeSyn, an evidence-grounded methodology that generates socially relevant syn- thetic queries by leveraging a fine-tuned taxonomy generator (TaG) anchored in real-world evidence. Evaluated against four mainstream LLMs, NodeSyn elicited failure rates up to five times higher than human-authored benchmarks. Ablation studies confirm that our granular taxonomic expansion significantly drives these failure rates, while independent validation reveals critical deficiencies in prominent guard models.

articles.title: GaP: A Graph-as-Policy Multi-Agent Self-Learning Harness For Variational Automation Tasks
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2607.05369v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For robots to work reliably in commercial and industrial applications, recent advances in agentic coding systems have potential to combine interpretable robot programming with the open-world adaptability of model-free policies. We focus on "Variational Automation" (VA), a class of tasks that have larger variations in object geometry and pose than fixed automation. Model-free policies often struggle to close the reliability gap for VA tasks, which must be executed persistently and reliably in commercial and industrial applications. Motivated by prior work on Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) and the Robot Operating System (ROS), we introduce Graph-as-Policy (GaP), a multi-agent coding harness that generates directed computation graphs with perception, planning, and control nodes from a Modular Open Robot Skill Library (MORSL). GaP generates an internal simulation environment to rehearse task instances with different graphs in parallel to iteratively refine the graph structure and parameters to improve success rates and throughput. Evaluation with 8 new open VA task benchmarks, 4 in simulation and 4 in real-world, suggests that GaP can achieve success rates that significantly outperform baselines. articles.title: Entity-Aware Evaluation of OCR Systems for Historical Document Transcription
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2610.33004v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is essential for digitizing historical archives, yet standard evaluation metrics such as Character Error Rate (CER) do not necessarily reflect whether meaningful information, such as names, dates, and identifiers, is preserved. In this work, we investigate entitylevel analysis of OCR errors as a complementary perspective for evaluating OCR quality in historical documents. Using a publicly available benchmark of 175 documents from the Berrutti Archive, augmented with 5,209 manually annotated entity mentions that will be released upon acceptance, we compare sequence-recognition OCR systems, OCR-specialized vision-language models, and general-purpose vision-language models. Beyond global transcription accuracy, we analyze entity preservation and recoverability under varying character-level edit tolerances. Our experiments show that OCR rankings depend on the evaluation criterion: while Qwen 3.6 achieves the highest entity coverage across all tested tolerances, several systems with lower exact-match coverage recover substantially when small errors are tolerated, suggesting that many of their errors correspond to localized character-level deviations rather than fundamentally incorrect entity transcriptions. Conversely, some systems remain unable to recover many entities even under relaxed matching. These findings show that OCR quality cannot be fully characterized by aggregate transcription metrics alone and highlight the importance of evaluating how OCR errors affect the preservation and recoverability of meaningful information.

articles.title: MedConstBench: Benchmarking How Constitutions Steer LLMs in Medical Ethics
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2610.36513v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: As large language models advance rapidly, they are increasingly used to answer medical questions, and many such models are now deployed locally. Once a model is deployed, its behavior is governed mainly by the ethical policy written into its constitution. However, most existing work focuses on factual correctness rather than the trade-off between competing ethical values. Even benchmarks that do evaluate ethics treat it as a fixed property of the model rather than as a variable, so how a constitution reshapes medical-ethics behavior remains largely unexplored. We introduce MedConstBench, a medical-ethics benchmark that treats the deployment constitution as a controlled variable, is organized around Beauchamp's four principles, and is scored by human-calibrated multi-model peer review. It includes MedDilemma, our own dataset of clinical dilemmas, and supports a systematic analysis of how constitutions steer LLMs. Evaluating ten open-source LLMs under four constitutions, we find that the effect of a constitution is dimension-selective and model-dependent, and that no constitution is universally optimal. Motivated by these findings, we propose a do-no-harm adaptive selector that chooses a constitution per model, matching the per-model oracle while guaranteeing a worst-case floor and generalizing to unseen models at low cost.

articles.title: Digital sovereignty in professional translation workflows: a case study of migrating from Windows to Linux
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2610.41561v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This study examines digital sovereignty in professional translation through a screening of computer-assisted translation tools and translation management systems, and a case study of migrating a translator's workstation from Windows to Linux. The framework combines three principles - Control, Continuity and Exit - with three practical requirements: native Linux operation, independence from mandatory external services, and independent access to essential data and resources. Drawing on documentary evidence and the limited number of responses received from providers, the ecosystem screening distinguishes Linux accessibility from operational independence: browser-based platforms may remain dependent on provider-controlled infrastructure. The migration case demonstrates the feasibility of reconstructing one professional workflow around a locally operable Linux core, using LoopCAT, LibreOffice and locally run TranslateGemma, alongside tools for optical character recognition, communication, credential management and backup. Selected cloud services remained available where needed. The findings suggest that digital sovereignty depends on how workflow dependencies are organized, rather than on individual applications or operating systems. It does not require technological isolation, but meaningful control over essential components, continuity of work and practical exit options. The framework is tailored to the case examined here and may require adaptation to other professional workflows.

articles.title: Where Is the "Self" of a Large Language Model? -- From Self-Index to Self-Reference
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2610.16717v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Whether a large language model has a self is usually argued without a way to measure it. We measure a functional self with two levels familiar from biology: a self-index, which marks material as the model's own, as animals tag self-generated signals with a corollary discharge, and self-reference, the ability to recognize what is one's own, as in mirror self-recognition. Our main finding is that language models mark their own messages in their internal representations and that recognizing these messages depends on this mark: no model we tested recognizes its own messages without it, and in the three models we edited, changing the mark removes or creates the recognition. We place the same text in an Assistant, a User, or a System message of the model's own chat template. In Qwen3.8-27B, the representation separates the model's own message from both external sources at every one of its 64 layers and in every held-out text. Asked who wrote a message, the model answers "you" with probability 0.77 for its own messages and at most 0.07 for the others. At each layer, we find eight directions along which the model's own message differs most from the same text as a User message. Giving the model's own message the User values along these directions lowers the rate of "you" to at most 0.05. Giving a User message the model's own values makes the model claim it, closing 41-67% of the gap between the two messages. Edits along eight random directions do neither. This holds in Qwen3.8-27B without and with thinking, gpt-oss-20b, and gpt-oss-120b. articles.title: Labadain-MedQA: A Tetun Medical QA Dataset for Fine-Tuning and Evaluating Large Language Models
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.00935v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Advances in large language models (LLMs) have created opportunities for cross-lingual transfer of medical knowledge from high-resource to low-resource languages to support access to healthcare information. However, medical question-answering (QA) datasets for fine-tuning and evaluating LLMs remain scarce for Tetun. To address this gap, we translated MedAlpaca's Medical Flashcards and WikiDoc Patient Information collections into Tetun using Gemini 2.5 Flash, producing 39,077 medical QA pairs. Translation quality was assessed on 50 randomly sampled QA pairs (100 documents) using automatic metrics against human reference translations and evaluations by two native Tetun-speaking healthcare professionals, focusing on medical accuracy and Tetun fluency. Human translations achieved higher mean ratings than LLM-generated translations for both criteria (4.43/5 vs. 4.02/5), with statistically significant differences (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p < 0.001). To assess downstream utility, we fine-tuned Gemma and Llama variants on the translated MedAlpaca dataset using parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) and evaluated them on 325 Tetun-translated United States Medical Licensing Examination multiple-choice questions. Gemma 4 12B fine-tuned using QLoRA achieved relative improvements in mean accuracy of 10.79% with 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) inference and 10.42% after merging the LoRA adapters into the BF16 base model, compared with the corresponding base models. These results highlight the viability of automatic dataset translation for Tetun medical QA and the effectiveness of PEFT in enhancing model performance. articles.title: Unsatz: Evaluating Scientific Discovery Without a Given Ansatz
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.03713v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Before a scientist fits any parameter, they must decide what the model contains: which quantities exist, which are hidden, how they interact, and how they are measured. Physicists call such a trial form an ansatz. Benchmarks for automated equation discovery mostly supply it, by fixing the variables, a library of candidate terms, or a law to be modified. We introduce Unsatz, a benchmark in which an LLM agent must construct the ansatz itself. Each task is a simulated system, generated from a private seed as a program in a small modeling language: ordinary, delay, or partial differential equations, discrete maps, static and causal models, or stochastic processes, possibly with hidden states, distorted sensors, and uninformative measurement channels. The agent buys experiments within a budget, writes candidate programs in the same language, obtains their coefficients from the benchmark's fitter, and is scored only on how its final program predicts experiments it never saw: conditions outside the range it could explore, interventions, and longer runs. Across 80 systems in 20 domains, nine language models solve between 21% and 60%. On 44 of these systems, classical equation-discovery methods almost never succeed, although the same data usually suffice once the true equations are given with unknown coefficients; the difficulty lies in finding the structure, not in estimating it. Because mechanisms recur across systems, we also give agents the program they discovered for a related system; it helped only when the new system shared the mechanism and the first investigation had succeeded. Stronger agents make fewer unscientific errors; beyond these, agents find which variables a system has but not how they act, and prefer revisions

articles.title: EMBERS: Empirically Motivated Robustness Testing of Deep Research Systems via Defect-Guided Fuzzing
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.03723v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep Research (DR) systems extend large language models into autonomous agents that decompose complex information needs, iteratively search the web, and synthesize evidence to answer challenging questions. However, their multi-stage execution may introduce robustness risks, as variations in user questions or intermediate search inputs may propagate across research stages and lead to incorrect answers. Existing evaluations focus on task-solving capabilities or robustness against external evidence disturbances, leaving intrinsic weaknesses in DR execution insufficiently explored. Thus, we conduct an empirical study of 1,932 execution trajectories from three representative DR systems and identify nine recurring defect categories across subquestion formulation, online search, and final reasoning. Guided by these findings, we propose EMBERS, an empirically motivated, defect-guided fuzzing framework for robustness testing of DR systems. Starting from correctly answered seed questions, EMBERS generates stage-targeted test inputs using defect-guided mutation, web-search-assisted fidelity assurance, and diversity-aware seed maintenance. Experiments across 16 framework--model--dataset settings show that EMBERS achieves 3.21 times the failure-discovery throughput of the strongest baseline under identical testing budgets. Human and LLM-assisted evaluations demonstrate that most generated inputs preserve the original information need and necessary contextual constraints. Moreover, model fine-tuning experiments show consistent-answer performance improvement, highlighting their value for robustness testing and model improvement.

articles.title: LaplaceDiag: Fault Diagnosis through Changes in Learned Actuator Effects
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.03849v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Identifying faulty components from sensor anomalies is difficult because fault effects can propagate through a plant and different faults can produce similar observations. Detailed component models and labeled fault examples may also be unavailable. We introduce LaplaceDiag, a data-driven method that uses changes in actuator effects to narrow the search for faulty equipment. Actuators act on specific devices and mechanisms, so their changed effects can provide clues to root causes. LaplaceDiag learns a healthy plant model with LaplaceNet, a neural network that operates in Laplace space. It separates nonlinear prediction based on measured history from an explicit matrix that describes how actuator values affect sensor values. Keeping the history predictor fixed allows current actuator effects to be estimated by linear regression without retraining the neural network. Comparison with a healthy reference accounts for estimation uncertainty and normal variation to detect changes and generate actuator-related diagnostic hypotheses. The method supports online and offline diagnosis, providing an intermediate step between anomaly detection and identifying faulty components. We successfully evaluate LaplaceDiag on two datasets.

articles.title: Predictive gains, causal losses: why interventional competence cannot be learned from data alone
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.03861v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Retaining predictive gains can require persistent errors in a model's response to interventions. For deterministic predictors with finite second moments under squared-error loss, any observational advantage over the best predictor using only an outcome's direct causes requires dependence on other inputs, regardless of the learning rule. When admissible interventions vary inputs while preserving the worldly outcome, this dependence yields a positive lower bound on root-mean-square intervention-response error. We identify conditions under which population gradient updates introduce this dependence from a parent-only baseline or damage a previously correct mechanism through shared parameters while improving other predictions. These dependencies can also make model behavior vary with how the same intervention is realized. We characterize interventional alignment through a common output mapping across internal states and physical processes realizing the same intervention target and relevant context. Correction is limited by the causal hypotheses currently admitted within inquiry. The relevant hypothesis class comprises these causal alternatives, rather than the function class the computational system could in principle represent. For predictions restricted to these alternatives, interventional mean error cannot fall below the best approximation they permit, whether evidence is observational or interventional. Reducing error below a positive limit requires admitting better hypotheses, which may entail revising the causal variables, mechanism structure, or intervention interpretation. articles.title: We Ran a Research Sprint With AI. The AI Worked. The Research Didn't
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.03946v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative AI tools for research are widely deployed, yet individual productivity gains do not guarantee better team research. We argue that how AI use is structured matters alongside access. Personal AI tools may amplify two failures under deadline pressure: a consumption bottleneck, in which generation outpaces team-visible evaluation, and AI-induced research silos, in which private human-AI loops displace shared decision-making. We motivate this position with a mechanism-generating pilot: a 100-minute research sprint with twelve researchers in three independently operating teams, within a seventeen-person session. Both patterns recurred across teams and evidence sources. Of 33 logged AI interactions, one was accepted outright and 27 lacked a recorded disposition; missing records alone do not establish absent evaluation. A parallel autonomous pipeline produced a complete draft without in-session human evaluation, illustrating production capacity rather than comparative quality. We propose Human-AI-Human collaboration: an interaction topology in which AI connects researchers' contexts and supports inspectable collective evaluation and decision-making. The pilot does not isolate AI-specific effects from time pressure or workflow practices. We close with seven modular, falsifiable design hypotheses, prioritizing shared context and team-visible evaluation checkpoints for controlled follow-up.

articles.title: Thinking Fast, Trading Late: System One Decision Models vs the Market
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.03985v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) read company news at scale, and backtests suggest that their readings predict stock returns. We ask how much of that predictability survives a test that rules out look-ahead, memorization and selection. We propose OLIVIA, a protocol for such tests: point-in-time inputs with company identities masked, selection on validation data only, an analysis plan frozen by cryptographic hash, and a test period unblinded once through a logged lock. We apply it to AI decision models, non-generative language models that return probabilities for typed questions, reading news about S&P 500 stocks: an open-weights model we fine-tuned on 2024-2025 data, three commercial models and standard baselines. The fine-tuned model's signal replicated on two validation quarters (daily information coefficients 0.055 and 0.065) but fell to 0.020 (t = 1.7) on the blinded January-July 2026 test. The commercial models' readings line up with the overnight move to the open (information coefficient 0.074 to 0.077) but not with the move after it, so the news is priced by the time a trader can act on it at the open. No model can tell over- from under-reaction, and no pre-registered strategy survives costs and a deflated Sharpe ratio. Commercial models identify masked companies in 62% to 74% of cases against a 28% baseline: masking hides names, not companies. The market reads the news first.

articles.title: WASP-Mem: Let Agent Organize Procedural Memory. Human Spend Effort on Diagnosis
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04003v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents struggle to automate complex enterprise procedures because static, pre-built harness cannot capture proprietary policies, undocumented behaviors, or state-dependent recovery paths that surface only during execution. Procedural memory accrued from agent experience offers a training-free path to closing this gap -- yet unlike episodic records or semantic facts, it must consolidate repeated successes and diagnosed failures into reusable actions and recovery strategies. We introduce WASP-Mem (Wiki-based Agent-Synthesized Procedural Memory), a nimble but effective method that distills execution traces and feedback into persistent, interlinked wiki pages, enabling continual agent learning. On TheAgentCompany benchmark, WASP-Mem raises the checkpoint pass rate by 4.6-6.1% over the strongest baseline we compared across three models while requiring 57-61% less storage. We further present a systematic controlled study spanning consolidation method, feedback type, trace ingestion scope, and refinement rounds. Our results reveal that prescriptive knowledge organization such as human defined schemas and explicit deduplication rules hurts performance rather than closing the procedural-knowledge gap. In contrast, human diagnosis converts failed traces into corrective knowledge and drives sustained improvement: a single round of human diagnosis outperforms four rounds of self-judgment by 7.0-10.9%. These findings point to a simple division of labor: let agents organize procedural memory, and invest human effort where it matters most -- diagnosis.

articles.title: Forgetting to Improve: Principled Data Removal in Active Learning
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04054v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The uncertainty of a statistical model is most commonly factorized into an aleatoric and an epistemic part. This factorization changes how predictions are interpreted in downstream decision tasks. Importantly, except for the idealistic scenario with no model mismatch, the quantification is a characteristic of the model and not the data generating process. In this paper, we propose Forgetting to Improve a method that reduces this discrepancy by incorporating the task into the modeling framework. Our key insight is to acknowledge that in scenarios of model mismatch, data can have a detrimental effect on the modeling for a specific task. Based on this insight, we propose an influence function for Gaussian process models that allows for principled removal of detrimental data samples. We showcase the flexibility of this approach by demonstrating significant improvements across a range of tasks, including Bayesian optimization, model-based reinforcement learning, and transductive learning.

articles.title: HybridSpec: Throughput-Aware Speculative Decoding for Hybrid GDN-MoE Models
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04055v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In speculative decoding, parallel drafters such as DFlash make drafting cheap, so target verification dominates each round. A central choice is the verification length, the number of tokens that the target processes in each round. Verifying more draft tokens can accept more of them, but work after the first rejection is wasted. For hybrid target models that combine Gated DeltaNet (GDN) and mixture-of-experts (MoE) layers, verification time grows much faster with this length than for dense models. In a single-request profile of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with DFlash, it grew by 71% from length 4 to 16, almost entirely in GDN and MoE layers, compared with 4%-6% for a dense Qwen3-4B target. Each GDN layer must update a recurrent state at every token and recover it at the end of the accepted prefix. The MoE cost depends on the experts that the tokens activate, which are known only once verification runs. We present HybridSpec, which selects the verification length on the GPU from draft-side acceptance estimates and measured target latency. Verification then runs this length plus one extra token up to the first MoE router, before any expert runs. There, a lightweight routing correction uses the observed expert assignments to decide whether to keep that token. The rest of verification runs only on the selected tokens. Block-parallel GDN kernels avoid storing a state after every token and reconstruct the accepted state of every GDN layer in one launch. In isolated benchmarks at verification lengths 4 to 16 with every draft token accepted, these kernels, including accepted-state reconstruction, are $1.54\times$-$4.04\times$ faster than the default kernels. articles.title: AlgoPilot: Cross-Paradigm Reasoning in Language Models via Strategy Selection and Guidance
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04079v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Real-world problems span diverse domains, including program synthesis, symbolic reasoning, planning, and optimization, and often require fundamentally different solution paradigms. A central challenge for LLM-based reasoning is twofold: identifying an appropriate problem-solving approach and formulating it correctly. In this paper, we propose AlgoPilot, a cross-paradigm reasoning framework that enables adaptive selection of the solving approaches and structured problem formulation prior to execution. The AlgoPilot framework contains three components: 1) a SteerLM, trained via supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL), that adaptively selects the solving strategy (paradigm and modes) based on input problems, 2) the corresponding expert GuideLM, trained via SFT, that generates structured formulation guidance tailored to the selected strategy, and 3) an ExecutionLM that generates solutions conditioned on both the selected strategy and its formulation. Unlike prompting-based methods that rely on fixed reasoning templates, our approach learns to adaptively choose and structure problem-solving strategies based on the input. We build AlgoPilot on Qwen3-8B and evaluate across 5 problem categories and 13 benchmarks with 66 unique domains, comparing against both the latest similarly scaled small models and large LLMs. AlgoPilot significantly improves average accuracy for the same model from 38.4% to 72.9%, outperforming the best large LLM prompting baseline GLM-5 by 11.7%. Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of each component. Notably, we show that the learned steering and formulation modules can transfer across execution models, suggesting their potential to improve other LLMs. Project page: https://site

articles.title: Contextual Linear Activation Steering of Language Models
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2604.24693v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Linear activation steering is a powerful approach for controlling and specializing large language models by adding linear representations of concepts to their activations at inference. While effective, existing methods often steer with a fixed strength, independent of how much steering any given input requires. In this work, we introduce Contextual Linear Activation Steering (CLAS), which decomposes activation steering into a fixed steering direction and a context-dependent steering coefficient. This decomposition preserves the interpretability of the steering direction while enabling the steering strength to vary with context. It also enables CLAS to perform selective steering: steering multiple behaviors across different portions of a single generation, which cannot be achieved using a fixed steering strength. In addition, across a wide range of steering benchmarks and language models, CLAS consistently outperforms standard linear activation steering and matches or exceeds ReFT and LoRA in settings with limited labeled data. Notably, CLAS achieves this using directions that also serve as reliable concept monitors, a property that directions learned via fine-tuning lack. We therefore propose CLAS as an interpretable and accurate method for controlling and specializing large language models.

articles.title: Learning Directional Randers Geometry for Latent-Space Exploration
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.03675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep neural networks extract powerful latent representations from images, enabling fast and efficient downstream analysis. However, these latent spaces lack explicit geometric structure, leading to possibly poor interpolation fidelity and misleading extrapolation. Latent interpolation techniques assume symmetric transition costs which are often not the case for real world data. Their symmetric nature cannot capture directional processes, such as disease progression, where certain transitions are impossible (e.g. tumor growth dynamics or cognitive improvement in Alzheimer's disease). Although Riemannian metrics extend Euclidean geometry by incorporating curvature, they remain symmetric. We show that understanding asymmetry and not curvature alone directly addresses these problems. To do so we propose a new Finsler-Randers metric learning framework. It incorporates direction-dependent distances, thus enabling the computation of trajectories respecting monotonic sequential constraints. We demonstrate its potential for interpolation and extrapolation on controlled cross-sectional datasets.

articles.title: From Forecasting to Feedback: Evaluating Learned Dynamics for Tokamak Control
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.03690v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learned temporal models are moving beyond offline forecasting toward interactive environments for decision making, yet logged-trajectory accuracy need not predict closed-loop behavior under policies optimized in the learned model. This forecasting-control gap matters in tokamak magnetic control, where coupled plasma-circuit dynamics and actuator constraints can amplify errors through feedback. Using a calibrated free-boundary Grad-Shafranov solver, we collect four datasets in a 2x2 design over physics-parameter and current-reference coverage. At matched budgets of 500, 1k, 3k, and 5k rollouts, we train 16 action-conditioned Transformers; PPO policies optimized in the 5k surrogates are then evaluated without adaptation on six reference-solver conditions. Only joint-coverage D4 shows monotonically decreasing cross-condition mean error, whereas D1 improves in distribution but degrades out of distribution. Binary completion masks substantial closed-loop differences: D2-D4 each complete 83.3% of conditions, but reach on average 99.0%, 94.7%, and 90.5% of the evaluation horizon, while their worst conditions reach 94.2%, 68.2%, and 43.2%. Policies trained with action noise complete 5/24 matched conditions, compared with 19/24 under nominal training, and have a lower mean horizon-capped episode length. Based on one trained policy per configuration and one evaluation realization per condition, the results support combining prediction error, episode completion, condition-level duration, and tracking quality.

articles.title: DualClusterNet: Personalized Pattern-Space Composition for Next-POI Recommendation
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.03726v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Next point-of-interest (POI) recommendation supports personalized place discovery on location-based Web platforms. Mobility routines can recur across users while being realized at different places and adapted to individual preferences. We present DualClusterNet, a causal sequential recommender that composes two population-shared prototype dictionaries. At each observed prefix, soft routers retrieve pattern and spatial mixtures; a factorized multiplicative interaction couples them, feature-wise affine modulation adapts the shared representation, and a separate user-conditioned branch with an additive--projective gate retains individual variation. The prediction head combines this representation with a learned first-order transition term and ranks the complete training POI vocabulary. We evaluate on NYC and TKY using a training-only vocabulary and an original-final-target protocol that neither bridges unknown POIs nor substitutes earlier targets. The available single-seed results show competitive full-candidate ranking, while controlled analyses support the contribution of the compositional and personalized branches. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/DualClusterNet-F4EE/.

articles.title: HyVox: Rethinking Low-Power Voice Intelligence towards Neuromorphic-von Neumann Edge Computing
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.03735v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present HyVox, a hybrid neuromorphic--von Neumann system for low-energy open-set speaker identification under tight energy budgets. HyVox splits the workload at the speaker embedding. A neuromorphic processor embeds the speech with sparse, event-driven computation, and a von Neumann microcontroller holds the speaker gallery and makes every decision: it scores queries by cosine similarity, rejects unknown speakers, and enrolls new users by writing a prototype, with no weight update. On the neuromorphic processor, a hierarchical temporal abstraction (HTA) SNN backbone learns a synaptic time constant per leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron, allocating 832 neurons across fast, medium, and slow timescales. A 32-neuron spiking embedding extractor (SEE), pretrained on episodes that each enroll new speakers and reject outsiders, turns the backbone output into an embedding for speakers unseen in training; its 32 spike counts are the only interface between the two processors. To fit the chip's synapse and integer budgets, we compress the backbone 6.5x to 29.0k synapses, train it for integer bit-shift dynamics, and fine-tune it with chip-accurate spiking training (CAST). CAST trains through a differentiable replica of the chip's integer neuron update, derived from its cycle-accurate simulator, so that gradient descent optimizes the exact weights and thresholds the chip runs; it doubles the top-1 accuracy of the mapped backbone on unseen speakers. On 20 Common Voice households of unseen speakers, HyVox reaches 99.6\% top-1 and 5.5\% rejection EER with 2 members and 94.9\% and 13.2\% with 20, and the network deployed on the neuromorphic chip matches its trained model. articles.title: The role of injected noise in diffusion model generalization
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.03764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diffusion models trained on distinct datasets can produce highly similar samples when prompted with the same noise input, suggesting that they learn a generalized data distribution. We investigate the role of noise injected during the sampling process, and show that it plays an important role in making or breaking this strong generalization effect. Based on this finding we investigate the robustness of sample similarity to changes in the injected noise, and find that its impact is largest in the sampling regime where broad structure already exists but the precise identity of the sample is not yet determined.

articles.title: Multi-layer Indexer: Overlapping Selection and Attention in DeepSeek Sparse Attention
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.03768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sparse attention cuts the cost of long-context inference by making the attention matrix sparse: each query attends only a subset of the sequence, chosen by a fixed pattern or, in recent production LLMs, learned per query. In DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA), the attention of DeepSeek-V3.2 and the GLM-5 family, every layer is preceded by a lightning indexer that scores the whole cache and keeps the k=2048 highest-scoring tokens for the layer to attend. At long context this indexer scan, not the sparse attention it feeds, is where the decode time goes. But adjacent layers select nearly the same tokens, so a layer can attend the selection of the previous indexer layer instead of its own. This removes the dependency: each indexer then runs concurrently with the attention of its layer. The resulting Multi-layer Indexer (MLI) needs no retraining and no new weights. Its default realization changes no kernel, running inside SGLang's production decode graph; an optional fused decode kernel accelerates it further on DeepSeek-V3.2. MLI composes with IndexCache (the cross-layer reuse GLM-5.2 ships as IndexShare): IndexCache drops the indexer from some layers, and MLI hides the scan on the rest. We serve DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5 under IndexCache's protocol at retentions 1/2 to 1/32 (the fraction of layers that keep an indexer) and contexts 10K to 195K. At equal retention the composition decodes faster than IndexCache: up to 14.5% faster on DeepSeek-V3.2 and 9.8% on GLM-5 at 1/2, and 7.9% and 5.1% at 1/4, largest where IndexCache keeps the most indexers and growing with context. articles.title: What Malware Actually Does: An Empirical Analysis of Post-Infection Behavior Across Malware Families
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.03774v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Most malware detection research focuses on identifying whether a file is malicious before it executes. Far less attention goes to what happens after infection. This paper presents an empirical analysis of post-infection malware behavior across 37 families, grounded in dynamic sandbox execution using CAPEv2. Behavioral traces are modeled as heterogeneous graphs with five node types and seven typed edge relationships, preserving relational structure that flat feature vectors discard. A voting ensemble trained on graph-derived structural features achieves 94.44% accuracy and MCC of 0.863, outperforming a flat behavioral baseline by 7.4 percentage points in MCC. A multiclass classifier distinguishes 24 malware families, and a per-family behavioral fingerprint analysis characterizes post-infection activity across registry, network, process, and API dimensions. An LLM explanation layer generates analyst-readable reports with MITRE ATT&CK mappings grounded in observed behavioral evidence. The full pipeline is deployed as HeteroScan at https://ama-andam.github.io/heteroscan.

articles.title: AIRoA-0: Long-Horizon, Precise, Cross-Embodiment Manipulation from Handheld Data
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.03815v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AIRoA-0 (A-0) is a bimanual manipulation system learned from 16,151 hours of handheld demonstrations, with no robot data collected at any stage. The demonstrations are recorded with YUBI, our open-source handheld gripper, which lets people record manipulation data anywhere with no robot present. From a single instruction, A-0 sorts more than a dozen small parts into their numbered cells and changes the mop pads and brush of a robot vacuum; among other tasks, it unzips a pencil case and folds a towel. It performs these tasks using only a camera on each wrist, with no head or scene camera, at a site where none of its training data was recorded. Across the ten tasks of our evaluation, it averages a success rate of 78%, against 27% for the strongest of four other vision-language-action models post-trained on the same task demonstrations. We collect no teleoperation data and use no reinforcement learning or on-robot corrections, and the robot appears only at test time. The system learns which regions of each wrist view matter for the task, predicts the stage the task has reached, and decodes actions as a continuous stream. A-0 is embodiment-agnostic: it runs on robots that mount the YUBI gripper, such as a bimanual Franka, TX-G2, OpenArm and UR. We are releasing the dataset, to our knowledge the largest open dataset of handheld-gripper demonstrations with task and subtask instructions, together with the pre-trained weights and the post-training recipe. Videos of A-0 on every task are on the project page, https://a-0.airoa.io. Anyone can build the gripper, record a task of their own and post-train the model on it in under four hours on a single node of eight H200 GPUs.

articles.title: PianoBench: Evaluating Musical Perception and Reasoning in Language Models
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.03839v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal language models continue to improve on broad music understanding benchmarks, but which musical features can they perceive and reason about? We investigate this question by introducing PianoBench, a benchmark that tasks language models with reasoning about musical performances across congruent acoustic and symbolic input representations. PianoBench is derived from our new multimodal, training-scale dataset comprising more than 20,000 hours of interleaved transcripts of music and spoken musical commentary from instructional piano videos. Open-weight audio-language models achieve at most 52.8% accuracy on PianoBench, and at best only modestly outperform their accuracy on a no-audio control. In contrast, frontier models using chain of thought achieve up to 93.2% accuracy when provided transcripts of music as text, exposing a gap between perceiving musical features from audio and reasoning about musical events when they are given explicitly. We then test whether mid-training on interleaved musical instruction can improve question answering without chain of thought, raising Qwen 3.5 9B Base's zero-shot accuracy on PianoBench with music transcripts from 42.8% to 56.0% after instruction tuning. These experiments suggest that instructional videos may represent an overlooked source of multimodal supervision for music. Available: https://gclef-cmu.org/pianobench.

articles.title: Camera Radar LiDAR Fusion via Point-Cloud Projection for Multi-Task Learning
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.03942v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autonomous vehicles require robust perception systems to operate safely under diverse environmental conditions. While cameras provide high-resolution visual data, their performance significantly degrades in low-light and adverse weather. High Definition (HD) radar offers superior reliability and angular resolution under such conditions but lacks rich visual feature recognition. LiDAR, though expensive, delivers highly precise distance measurements and dense point clouds. Each sensor exhibits unique trade-offs, necessitating the development of advanced sensor fusion algorithms to harness complementary strengths while minimizing computational complexity and maintaining accuracy. In this study, the proposed fusion architecture performs early fusion by combining camera images with perspective-view point cloud data from HD radar and LiDAR sensors. The proposed model is trained to detect vehicles and segment free drivable space simultaneously. Experiments are performed on the RADIal dataset where we demonstrate that fusing point cloud data with camera images in front-view surpasses the performances of the most recent standalone and fusion models.

articles.title: P$^2$-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.03953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation consolidates expert capabilities by supervising student-generated trajectories, whereas task arithmetic offers a training-free alternative through linear parameter combinations. We view the linear combination of student and expert parameters as a single differentiable model and propose P$^2$-MOPD, which jointly optimizes the mixing coefficients and the student weights under the same on-policy distillation objective. Unlike task arithmetic, which stays within the span of the frozen student and expert parameters for any choice of merging coefficients, P$^2$-MOPD keeps the student trainable, so the experts act as parameter priors without confining it to this span. Across four domains at 1.7B and 4B scales, P$^2$-MOPD achieves faster and more balanced recovery than MOPD from the same initialization, surpassing its final average recovery in half the training steps. At the end of training, our 1.7B model reaches 94.7% average recovery, versus 80.9% for MOPD.

articles.title: Stacking-Based Weighting for Large Language Bayes in M-Open Settings
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.03966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Bayes (LLB) transforms a natural language problem description into a collection of candidate probabilistic programs and performs inference within each model, combining their predictions using Bayesian model averaging. While this provides a flexible framework for probabilistic inference without manual model specification, the resulting candidate model set is often misspecified in practice, and likelihood-based aggregation can concentrate on a single model, under-representing uncertainty across the sampled models. We propose a stacking-based aggregation method for LLB that selects model weights by optimizing predictive performance rather than marginal likelihood, while preserving the original language-model-driven model generation and within-model inference pipeline. Because leave-one-out predictive quantities are intractable in latent-variable models, we derive a variational lower bound that yields a tractable ELBO-based stacking objective. Across real-world probabilistic inference tasks, our method achieves comparable predictive performance to Bayesian model averaging while yielding more dispersed model weights, reducing concentration on a single candidate model under misspecification.

articles.title: FlagRot: Selective Rotation for Low-Bit KV Caches
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.03992v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-context inference is bound by the KV cache, which 2-bit codes could shrink about sixfold if their error stays in check. The usual remedy rotates keys before quantizing, assuming rotation always helps. However, we observe that it does not: rotation flattens a spiky piece of a key but can give a flat one a new peak, and both coexist within one key. We therefore propose FlagRot, which stores each 32-channel piece rotated or as is, whichever has the smaller calibrated attention error, and rotates the query instead when reading. We further show that how often to decide follows the quantization axis: per-channel caches such as KIVI need one decision per head, at no write cost, while per-token caches decide per key, with the choice stored in existing sign bits. At 2.5 bits per value, FlagRot lowers the twelve-model KL divergence of KIVI from 18.7 to 12.4 x 10^-3, below RotateKV on 9 of 12 models. Served as a vLLM plugin, it raises RULER at 128k tokens by +2.9 points and the LongBench v1 mean by +0.4 to +1.9 points on the three of four models where 2-bit KIVI loses accuracy. It also lowers the error of 4-bit integer and FP4 caches.

articles.title: Separating Common and Unique Directions for Model Merging
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04108v2 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model merging combines multiple fine-tuned models without additional training, and arithmetic methods have emerged as a simple yet effective way to merge models without data. However, existing arithmetic methods treat task vectors in parameter space and apply a single element-wise rule to directions that can differ in mergeability. In a shared directional basis, we find a consistent two-regime structure: a low-dispersion common bulk shared across tasks and a high-dispersion task-dominated tail that carries disproportionate energy. These findings motivate Common--Unique Subspace Decomposition (CUSD), a data-free pre-merging method that separates task vectors into common and unique directional components, merges the common components with a downstream arithmetic operator, and retains unique residuals separately. Experiments across $11$ base models, four model families, and four arithmetic-based merging operators show that CUSD improves 42 of 44 model--operator combinations and achieves up to 22.5% improvement over the corresponding baselines. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/stwang666/CUSD

articles.title: What Remains in Sight? Autoregressive Video Decoding as Representation-Guided Context Rewriting
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04164v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-horizon video generation is increasingly moving toward autoregressive rollout, where each newly generated segment becomes part of the evidence used for future prediction. Recent causal decoders, long-context training, and KV-cache mechanisms have extended feasible duration, but most inference pipelines still decide the visible past implicitly through recent windows, compressed caches, or external memory. This raises a direct question: \textbf{can the choice of which past frames or segments to show to the decoder be treated as an explicit test-time decision?} We answer this question with \textsc{ReCR}, a training-free method that formulates autoregressive video decoding as representation-guided context rewriting. At each step, \textsc{ReCR} builds a selected visible context from the generated history by using internal decoder representations to favor context units that match the global rollout state, avoid redundancy with the recent continuation, preserve temporal boundary coverage, and widen the range of spatial layouts in view. The selected units are then mapped onto a compact causal axis before decoding the next block. Across long-horizon text-to-video benchmarks, \textsc{ReCR} consistently improves multiple autoregressive backbones under matched visible-token budgets. Empirical analyses such as representation-space diagnostics and transition-count prompt switching further show that improving what remains visible is an effective path toward more stable long-video decoding.

articles.title: Impact of Input Resolution in Mammographic Mass Detection: A Controlled Multi-Architecture Study
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04200v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep-learning-based mass detectors usually downsample mammograms, trading fine image detail for lower computational cost. However, published studies cannot reveal how much accuracy this trade-off sacrifices, since they also differ in architecture, preprocessing, and evaluation protocol. In this work, we isolated the effect of input resolution in a controlled study on the VinDr-Mammo dataset, training 18 detectors at six input resolutions ranging from 512 x 416 to 1600 x 1280 pixels, for 108 model-resolution combinations. Whole mammograms were resized without cropping or tiling. For each model, preprocessing, model initialization, augmentation, and evaluation procedures were kept fixed across resolutions. Detection accuracy was evaluated by mAP50 on the 219 mass-positive images of the official test split, and 57 combinations with test mAP50 of at least 0.60 were analyzed. From the lowest to the highest resolution, median mAP50 rose from 0.626 to 0.660 and the best mAP50 from 0.670 to 0.709. The best result, achieved by DINO with a ConvNeXt-S backbone, is the highest mAP50 reported to date on mass-positive VinDr-Mammo images. Gains were concentrated in small masses: for the smallest third of lesions, median mAP50 rose by 0.074 (from 0.367 to 0.441), compared with 0.007 and 0.032 for medium and large masses. Median training time increased from 0.45 to 1.40 h, and median inference time from 23.6 to 113.7 ms per image. Therefore, higher input resolution mainly benefits the small masses that are hardest to detect, at a computational cost that remains practical.

articles.title: GC-MoE: Overlapping Expert-Parallel Token Dispatch with FP8/FP4 Grouped GEMM via CUDA Green Contexts
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04222v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Under expert parallelism, mixture-of-experts (MoE) layers pay all-to-all token dispatch, grouped GEMMs, and a combine step in every layer. In decode each rank holds only 1-256 tokens: dispatch latency and weight traffic dominate while tensor-core utilization is inherently low. In fused operators such as DeepGEMM's Mega MoE, dispatch and computation overlap only by sharing every SM: dispatch warps compete with TMA/MMA and epilogue warps for registers, shared memory, and issue slots; every phase shares one CTA resource budget, synchronization spans the whole SM array, and every replay ends with a workspace-clean pass and a cross-rank barrier. We present GC-MoE, an open-source FP8/FP4 MoE inference operator for NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell GPUs that uses CUDA Green Contexts to split the device into a small communication partition and a large compute partition. Each role gets its own kernel, resource budget, and synchronization domain, so dispatch and GEMM tune independently. The compute partition runs operand-swapped tcgen05 block-scaled MMA on Blackwell and register-A WGMMA with in-register FP4 decoding on Hopper, with fused SwiGLU, requantization, and optional shared experts. articles.title: LIRA: A More Interpretable Dynamic Loss-Informed Rank Allocation for Low-Rank Adaptation
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04239v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) has become a widely used parameter-efficient fine-tuning method for large pretrained models. However, standard LoRA typically assigns a fixed rank profile despite layer- and stage-dependent adaptation needs, while recent adaptive-rank variants often rely on heuristic or first-order signals that provide only an indirect link between rank reallocation and local loss behavior. This leaves the rationale behind each rank reallocation insufficiently interpretable. Motivated by this gap, we propose LIRA (Loss-Informed Rank Allocation), a dynamic-rank LoRA method designed to make online rank reallocation more interpretable. LIRA scores each layer by the estimated magnitude of the local loss perturbation associated with its recent LoRA-factor movements under a second-order approximation, making the basis for each rank change interpretable term by term. By periodically applying DELTA (Displacement-Evaluated Loss-Trajectory Allocation), a displacement-based algorithm for LoRA rank reallocation, LIRA produces discrete effective ranks under matched budgets while remaining compatible with standard (A,B) adapters. On RoBERTa-base GLUE under the La-LoRA/LoRA protocol, LIRA outperforms the uniform-LoRA and adaptive-rank baselines reported under this protocol; Trajectory EMA attains performance competitive with Fixed-point Fisher at lower estimation cost.

articles.title: OmniST: Topology-Invariant Spatiotemporal Forecasting with Guaranteed-Coverage Uncertainty at Unseen Sensor Locations
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04256v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Standard spatiotemporal graph convolutional networks need a fixed-size adjacency matrix, coupling model weights to a specific sensor count N; they cannot produce any output at a sensor absent from training. We present OmniST, a topology-invariant forecaster whose computation has zero structural dependency on the number of nodes, and which, composed with inductive split-conformal calibration, gives distribution-free, coverage-guaranteed prediction intervals at arbitrary (including never-seen) sensor locations, preserving that guarantee as sensors are added or removed. Topology invariance follows from coordinate-based tokenization, k-nearest-neighbor attention from geographic coordinates at each forward pass, and per-node temporal processing via a bidirectional GRU. On real Delhi air-quality data (37 stations, 2019-2023), OmniST attains a 30-day PM2.5 MAE of 31.0 ug/m3 and degrades at most 1.1 percent when 40 percent of stations are removed. Its inductive forecasts at unseen stations beat nearest-neighbor interpolation (about 12 percent) and a learned kriging GNN (IGNNK, about 21 percent), and, unlike either, carry a finite-sample coverage guarantee. The guarantee holds at 90 percent or above under 30-50 percent node dropout across four real datasets over three domains (Delhi and Beijing air quality, NOAA GHCN weather, Caltrans PeMSD7-M traffic), and still holds at 325 real sensors (full PeMS-BAY). We also fix a temporal-drift failure: static conformal under-covers over time (about 0.50 late), but a rolling adaptive-conformal estimator restores target coverage (0.89 overall, 0.96 late) at the cost of wider intervals.

articles.title: Reciprocity Can Erase Direction:tructural Boundaries and Controlled Utility of Magnetic Graph Networks
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetic graph networks encode direction through phase, but a learned graph can erase the intended directional mechanism before prediction. We characterize this failure for support-based magnetic Laplacians. Exact identities relate imaginary energy and distance from zero phase to amplitude-weighted reciprocity. Top-$k$ selection forces complete collapse when the observed-node count satisfies $m\leq k+1$, and dense support imposes a lower bound on reciprocal-arc fraction. We then construct paired propagation examples with identical node features and symmetric amplitudes but opposite labels, giving a provable chance-level limit for direction-erasing representations. In 72 fixed neural fits, support phase achieved test AUROC 1.0000 on a unilateral ring but 0.5000 on reciprocal ring and complete supports; continuous score phase and a real directed comparator achieved 1.0000 throughout. All models solved the direction-free control. These are oracle-direction mechanism tests, not evidence of learned clinical direction. In the preserved public DeepDRiD development study, continuous phase was active but its robustness difference from zero phase was only $+0.0036$ (descriptive 95\% interval $-0.0014$ to $+0.0095$) on validation patients used for checkpoint selection. The contribution is a structural and experimental framework for distinguishing erased direction from unestablished task utility. It provides a precise circumstance in which magnetic phase preserves useful information, without asserting universal or clinical superiority.

articles.title: What Is the Influence of Task Order in Continual Learning? An Empirical Study and Order-Aware Evaluation for Motion Forecasting
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.04309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aggregate scores for continual learning algorithms rest on a distribution over task orders that is rarely stated. We formulate algorithm comparison as an expectation over a declared order distribution, which separates training variation from order variation, and apply it to motion forecasting with four road-layout tasks from the INTERACTION dataset, all 24 task orders, four algorithms, and three training replicates (288 runs). Task order accounts for 65\% to 91\% of the variation in current-task error and backward transfer, and 90\% to 99\% of this order effect comes from the identity of the starting task: the smallest task cannot be learned from a cold start. Beyond the first stage, the order effect is comparable to training variability. In most orders, the leading algorithm in current-task error and backward transfer is within one replicate standard deviation of the runner-up. Backward transfer depends on the order mainly through its reference term, which weights the first task most heavily, so relative improvement and final error identify different leading algorithms for displacement error. A transition-direction descriptor computed from task statistics tracks the position of the smallest task, and weighting orders by it leaves the algorithm ranking unchanged. These results call for benchmarks that declare their order distribution and report order-resolved, starting-task-resolved, warm-start, and final errors alongside aggregate scores. The code and data are available \href{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/task-order-cl-4f7b/}{here}.
